points.title: 童年启蒙
points.description: 1847年2月11日，托马斯·爱迪生出生于俄亥俄州米兰市。他是家中七个孩子中最小的一个。童年时期，爱迪生表现出强烈的好奇心，对科学实验充满热情。由于他经常提问且被认为注意力不集中，仅接受了三个月正规教育后便在家由母亲教导。这段时期他阅读了大量书籍，包括科学和化学著作，并在家中地下室建立了小型实验室，开始进行各种实验。这段早期经历培养了他独立思考和动手实践的能力，为他日后的发明生涯奠定了基础。
points.descriptionEn: Thomas Edison was born on February 11, 1847, in Milan, Ohio, the youngest of seven children in a family of Dutch and Canadian descent. As a child, Edison exhibited intense curiosity and a passion for scientific experiments. Due to his constant questioning and perceived inattentiveness, he received only three months of formal education before being homeschooled by his mother. During this period, he read extensively, particularly in science and chemistry, and set up a small laboratory in his basement where he conducted various experiments. This early experience fostered his independent thinking and hands-on practical abilities, laying the foundation for his future career as an inventor.

points.title: 电报生涯
points.description: 12岁时，爱迪生因听力问题辍学，开始在火车上售卖报纸和糖果。16岁时，他成为一名电报操作员，这一职业开启了他的技术生涯。在休伦港期间，他改进了电报技术，发明了自动电报机，能够同时发送多条消息。1868年，他发明了电子投票记录仪，虽然国会未采用，但这是他的第一个专利。这段经历使爱迪生意识到发明可以商业化，并开始将技术创新与市场需求相结合。他的电报工作也让他结识了重要的人脉，为他日后的事业发展奠定了基础。
points.descriptionEn: At age 12, Edison's hearing problems led him to drop out of school, and he began selling newspapers and candy on trains. At 16, he became a telegraph operator, a profession that launched his technical career. During his time in Port Huron, Edison improved telegraph technology and invented the automatic telegraph, capable of sending multiple messages simultaneously. In 1868, he invented the electronic vote recorder, though it was not adopted by Congress, this was his first patent. This experience made Edison realize that inventions could be commercialized, and he began to combine technological innovation with market demands. His telegraph work also connected him with important contacts, laying the foundation for his future career development.

points.title: 发明创业
points.description: 1869年，爱迪生移居纽约，开始了他的发明创业生涯。他最初为金融公司改进了股票行情自动收录器，并以此获得了4万美元的初始资金。1870年，他成立了爱迪生精密仪器公司，开始生产改良的股票行情机。1874年，他发明了四工式电报机，能够同时传输四条消息。1876年，他在新泽西州门洛帕克建立了世界上第一个工业研究实验室，这是他最重要的创新之一。这个实验室采用系统化的方法进行发明创造，雇佣了多名科学家和技术人员，为现代企业研发模式奠定了基础。在纽约期间，爱迪生确立了'发明工厂'模式，将科学研究与商业应用紧密结合。
points.descriptionEn: In 1869, Edison moved to New York and began his career as an inventor and entrepreneur. Initially, he improved the stock ticker for financial companies and received $40,000 in initial funding. In 1870, he established the Edison Precision Instrument Works and began producing improved stock tickers. In 1874, he invented the quadruplex telegraph, capable of transmitting four messages simultaneously. In 1876, he established the world's first industrial research laboratory in Menlo Park, New Jersey, which became one of his most important innovations. This laboratory used systematic methods for invention, employing multiple scientists and technicians, laying the foundation for the modern corporate R&D model. During his time in New York, Edison established the 'invention factory' model, closely integrating scientific research with commercial applications.

points.title: 发明黄金期
points.description: 门洛帕克时期是爱迪生发明生涯的黄金时代。在这里，他获得了1093项专利，平均每10天就有一项发明诞生。1877年，他发明了留声机，这是他最著名的发明之一，能够记录和播放声音。1878年，他开始研究电灯，经过数千次实验，1879年成功发明了实用白炽灯泡，并建立了电力系统。1880年，他成立了爱迪生电灯公司，后来发展成为通用电气公司。1882年，他在纽约建立了第一个商业电力系统，为曼哈顿下城提供电力。门洛帕克实验室成为全球创新的中心，吸引了来自世界各地的参观者和投资者。这一时期确立了爱迪生作为'门洛帕克的奇才'的声誉，他的发明彻底改变了人们的生活方式和工业生产。
points.descriptionEn: The Menlo Park period represented the golden age of Edison's inventive career. Here, he obtained 1,093 patents, averaging one invention every ten days. In 1877, he invented the phonograph, one of his most famous inventions, capable of recording and playing sound. In 1878, he began researching electric lighting, and after thousands of experiments, successfully invented the practical incandescent light bulb in 1879, establishing an electrical system. In 1880, he founded the Edison Electric Light Company, which later became General Electric. In 1882, he established the first commercial electrical system in New York, providing power to downtown Manhattan. The Menlo Park laboratory became a global center of innovation, attracting visitors and investors from around the world. This period established Edison's reputation as the 'Wizard of Menlo Park,' and his inventions revolutionized people's lifestyles and industrial production.

points.title: 晚年创新
points.description: 1887年，爱迪生将实验室迁至西奥兰治，建立了更大的发明工厂，占地24英亩。在这里，他继续进行各种发明研究，包括电影摄影机和放映机（1891年发明 kinetoscope），并创立了爱迪生电影制片公司。他还开发了蓄电池、水泥制造方法和矿石分离技术等。晚年，爱迪生将更多精力投入到工业应用和商业推广中，他的发明工厂成为现代研发中心的典范。尽管面临听力障碍，爱迪生仍然保持活跃的工作状态，每天工作长达18小时。1929年，他参加了白宫为庆祝电灯发明50周年举行的庆典，亨利·福特为他重建了门洛帕克实验室。1931年10月18日，爱迪生在西奥兰治逝世，享年84岁，美国全国熄灯一分钟以示哀悼。
points.descriptionEn: In 1887, Edison moved his laboratory to West Orange, establishing a larger invention factory spanning 24 acres. Here, he continued various invention research, including the movie camera and projector (inventing the kinetoscope in 1891), and founded the Edison Manufacturing Company. He also developed storage batteries, cement manufacturing methods, and ore separation techniques. In his later years, Edison devoted more energy to industrial applications and commercial promotion, and his invention factory became a model for modern R&D centers. Despite his hearing impairment, Edison remained active with a work schedule of up to 18 hours daily. In 1929, he attended a celebration at the White House marking the 50th anniversary of the electric light, where Henry Ford had reconstructed the Menlo Park laboratory for him. On October 18, 1931, Edison died in West Orange at the age of 84, and the nation observed a moment of darkness for one minute in his honor.

appraisal.zh: 爱迪生通常被视为工业革命的关键人物和现代创新体系的奠基者，他拥有1093项美国专利，留声机、电灯等发明改变了现代生活，其建立的工业研究实验室模式开创了现代企业研发的先河。不过也有研究者指出，他的成功很大程度上依赖团队协作与系统化方法，而非个人天才的神话；在电流战争中为推广直流电而诋毁交流电的做法，以及许多发明实为对他人想法的改进，也使他的原创性受到质疑。
appraisal.en: Edison is generally seen as a key figure of the Industrial Revolution and a founder of the modern innovation system, holding 1,093 U.S. patents and changing modern life with the phonograph and electric light, while his industrial research laboratory pioneered corporate R&D. Yet some researchers note that his success rested heavily on teamwork and systematic methods rather than the myth of individual genius, and that his campaign against alternating current and his many improvements on others' ideas raise questions about his originality.

supporter.zh: 爱迪生被誉为'门洛帕克的奇才'和'发明大王'，是人类历史上最伟大的发明家之一。他拥有1093项美国专利，创造了留声机、电灯、电影摄影机等改变世界的发明。爱迪生体现了美国梦的精神，通过不懈努力和创造力改变了现代生活。他建立的工业研究实验室模式开创了现代企业研发的先河，影响了整个科技产业的发展。爱迪生不仅是一位发明家，更是一位企业家，他懂得如何将创新转化为商业价值，这种能力使他成为工业革命的关键人物。
supporter.en: Edison is hailed as the 'Wizard of Menlo Park' and the 'King of Inventors,' one of the greatest inventors in human history. He held 1,093 U.S. patents and created world-changing inventions such as the phonograph, electric light, and motion picture camera. Edison embodied the American Dream spirit, transforming modern life through relentless effort and creativity. The industrial research laboratory model he established pioneered modern corporate R&D, influencing the development of the entire technology industry. Edison was not just an inventor but also an entrepreneur who understood how to transform innovation into commercial value, making him a key figure of the Industrial Revolution.

critic.zh: 爱迪生的发明方法也存在争议。他常被批评过度依赖团队工作，而非个人天才；他的'99%汗水'名言掩盖了系统化研究和团队协作的重要性。在电流战争中，爱迪生为推广直流电而诋毁交流电，甚至用交流电处死动物以证明其危险性，这种商业竞争手段被批评为不道德。此外，爱迪生对尼古拉·特斯拉等竞争对手的打压也显示出他商业竞争中的阴暗面。他的许多发明实际上是对他人想法的改进而非原创，如电话和电影技术，这引发了对他的原创性真实性的质疑。
critic.en: Edison's inventive methods have also faced criticism. He is often accused of relying excessively on teamwork rather than individual genius; his '99% perspiration' quote obscures the importance of systematic research and collaboration. During the War of Currents, Edison discredited alternating current to promote direct current, even using AC to electrocute animals to demonstrate its dangers, a tactic criticized as unethical. Furthermore, Edison's suppression of competitors like Nikola Tesla reveals the darker side of his business practices. Many of his inventions were actually improvements on others' ideas rather than original creations, such as the telephone and motion picture technology, raising questions about the authenticity of his originality.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，爱迪生被定义为工业革命的关键人物和现代创新体系的奠基者。他不仅是一位发明家，更是将科学转化为实用技术的先驱。爱迪生建立的工业研究实验室模式成为现代企业研发的标准范式，影响了整个20世纪的科技创新。他的发明改变了人类的生活方式，从照明到娱乐，从通信到工业生产。爱迪生形象已成为美国创新精神的象征，代表着坚持不懈、实用主义和商业头脑的结合。然而，历史学家也认识到，他的成功很大程度上依赖于团队协作和系统化方法，而非个人天才的神话。爱迪生的一生反映了19世纪末到20世纪初美国技术发展的黄金时代。
objective.en: In historical scholarship and popular culture, Edison is defined as a key figure of the Industrial Revolution and the founder of the modern innovation system. He was not just an inventor but a pioneer in transforming scientific knowledge into practical technology. The industrial research laboratory model he established became the standard paradigm for modern corporate R&D, influencing technological innovation throughout the 20th century. His inventions transformed human lifestyles, from lighting to entertainment, from communication to industrial production. The Edison image has become a symbol of American innovative spirit, representing perseverance, pragmatism, and business acumen. However, historians also recognize that his success relied heavily on teamwork and systematic methods rather than the myth of individual genius. Edison's life reflects the golden age of American technological development from the late 19th to early 20th century.

self.zh: 天才是百分之一的灵感加上百分之九十九的汗水。
self.en: Genius is one percent inspiration and ninety-nine percent perspiration.
